title: Seed fcitx5 DefaultIM from vconsole XKBLAYOUT
head: f58750fd1f19
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Seed writes a different profile from the one fcitx5 reads when XDG_CONFIG_HOME or FCITX_CONFIG_HOME is set
leads.consequence: With XKBLAYOUT=fr and XDG_CONFIG_HOME different from $HOME/.config, the helper reports changed and may stop/restart fcitx5, but fcitx5 continues to read its keyboard-us profile from $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/fcitx5/profile (or $FCITX_CONFIG_HOME/profile). The migration is marked done, and rerunning the helper considers the orphan $HOME/.config/fcitx5/profile already correct.
leads.triage: dropped_private; pre-existing code, reviewed twice; XDG/FCITX config vars not set by Omarchy; low value for follow-up

leads.summary: One-item profile with a custom Item Layout or group name is misclassified as stock and overwritten
leads.consequence: A user who kept keyboard-us as DefaultIM but set the sole item's Layout=de, renamed the group, or changed GroupOrder has made a real fcitx5 customization. On a non-US vconsole the helper replaces the whole file and silently discards those fields. Its only stock checks are DefaultIM, Default Layout, item count and name.
leads.triage: verified_private; fcitx5 instance.cpp:535-559 confirms item Layout overrides keymap; pre-existing, narrow customisation; kept in REPORT

leads.summary: A partial profile write makes the migration succeed without repair on retry
leads.consequence: If writing an existing stock profile truncates it then fails mid-stream (disk full, I/O fault), the first helper exits nonzero, so migration does not restart fcitx5 or write its marker. On retry the partial file exists but does not look stock, so the helper exits 0 without changed; the migration exits 0 and is marked completed although the partial profile remains. fcitx5 may fall back to keyboard-us. Write via a temp file and rename only on success, and make an interrupted seed recoverable.

leads.summary: Related open PR #9565 skips its layout sync for this PR's seeded non-US profiles
leads.consequence: If both diverged open PRs merge, a fresh non-US installation receives one-item keyboard-fr, Default Layout=fr; #9565's first-run manager only adopts an unmarked group when its default is keyboard-us / us. It therefore returns without adding engines or synchronizing the multiple Hyprland layouts for such installs, despite the group still being created by Omarchy. Teach that predicate to recognize this seed, or coordinate the two PRs.

leads.summary: A failed pgrep probe is treated as absence and can still write over a live fcitx5
leads.consequence: If systemctl reports the service active but stop fails, and pgrep cannot inspect the process (missing or failing procps, fatal exit 3), both the wait and final guard interpret nonzero as 'gone'; pkill failures are also masked. The script writes and prints changed while the live daemon may overwrite the profile afterward. Distinguish pgrep's no-match exit 1 from probe errors 2/3, and fail closed when stop cannot be confirmed.
leads.triage: dropped; pgrep error exit edge case

leads.summary: The new guard treats a zombie fcitx5 as still running and blocks migrations
leads.consequence: After the process has actually exited and can no longer save a profile, an unreaped zombie with comm=fcitx5 still matches pgrep -x (no runstate filter). The ten waits and final guard exit 1; a pending migration never gets its marker, stops later migrations in omarchy-migrate and retries on subsequent updates until the zombie is reaped. The installer leaf similarly fails finalization. Filter zombie state or use a verified running-process check.
leads.triage: dropped; zombie transient under systemd reaping

leads.summary: Runtime-finalization docs omit the new fcitx5 seed leaf
leads.consequence: The source-of-truth list for omarchy-provision-user says install/user/all.sh runs theme, chromium, git, xcompose, mise and keyring, but omits fcitx5-layout.sh. Add the fcitx5 layout seed to that list for accurate install/reset guidance.

leads.summary: The new test does not exercise the new still-running guard
leads.consequence: Every helper run defaults FCITX_PGREP=1, even the 'active' case: no test has pgrep still matching after the ten waits. Removing the four-line final pgrep guard at helper:152-155 leaves all 13 test assertions passing. Add stop-failure or still-running case asserting nonzero, unchanged profile, no changed output, and no restart/marker as appropriate.
leads.triage: corroborates; same as N3 (Opus mutant run agrees)

leads.summary: Duplicate vconsole keys select a different layout from Hyprland
leads.consequence: With two valid XKBLAYOUT assignments, e.g. us followed by fr, Hyprland's reader sets values[key] for each line and uses fr; helper prints the first matching value and exits, sees us and skips seed. Conversely first fr then us causes helper to seed fr while compositor uses us. Same mismatch applies to repeated XKBVARIANT. Read the last assignment as the compositor does.

leads.summary: Potential migration-time XIM restart conflict with open PR #9568
leads.consequence: #9568 deliberately defers an unattended migration's fcitx5 restart because X11 clients may retain XIM objects and crash later. This PR still stops/restarts fcitx5 in its migration when a graphical session is active. Both PRs can coexist textually, but the proposed safety policy may be undermined; confirm against a live XIM client (e.g. Steam) or its reconnect implementation before posting as a runtime bug.

limits: No X11/XIM client source or live client was evaluated for H10, so it remains a hypothesis. Full test/all was not run because it executes unrelated desktop/package scripts; focused new test and CLI metadata probe ran in review.py.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [previous review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12920#issuecomment-5855762079) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12920#issuecomment-5857410868), checked at `f58750fd1f19`.

**Resolved:** the main part of the earlier finding "Stop failures still report `changed`". When this user's fcitx5 outlives the wait, [`bin/omarchy-fcitx5-seed-layout:152-155`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/f58750fd1f19a793b106f857e6e844adeb0760c2/bin/omarchy-fcitx5-seed-layout#L152-L155) now exits 1 without writing or printing `changed`, so the migration stays pending and is retried. The reply's description is accurate. The earlier stop-before-write fix is unchanged.

**Verified:** sandboxed runs with real `pgrep`/`pkill` against a fixture-owned process named `fcitx5` that saves a stock US profile 2 s after SIGTERM:

| Slow-exit stand-in | Previous head `f28b2652` | Current head `f58750fd` |
|---|---|---|
| Helper | prints `changed`, writes FR | exits 1 after about 1 s, no write |
| Profile after the late save | keyboard-us | keyboard-us (unchanged) |
| `omarchy-migrate` | marks `1790096150.sh` applied | stays pending, retried next run |

The new check also introduces one regression, described below. The earlier review suggested this check without scoping it to the current user.

## The new exit also fires for another user's fcitx5

`pgrep -x fcitx5` on [lines 144, 149 and 152](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/f58750fd1f19a793b106f857e6e844adeb0760c2/bin/omarchy-fcitx5-seed-layout#L143-L155) matches every user's processes. `pkill -x fcitx5` cannot signal another user's process, and `|| true` hides that failure.

```text
Second user's desktop session open, this user on a non-US console with a stock US profile:
  helper: stop this user's unit -> pkill cannot stop the other fcitx5
       -> pgrep still matches after about 1 s -> exit 1, profile not written
  migration: `changed=$(...)` fails -> omarchy-migrate exits, marker not written
             -> later migrations do not run; this user's fcitx5 stays stopped
  installer step: omarchy-provision-user (set -euo pipefail) exits at fcitx5-layout.sh,
                  before mise-work.sh
```

At `f28b2652` the same case completed: the profile was written, and the migration was recorded and restarted fcitx5 in a desktop session. That result was correct, because the other user's fcitx5 saves its profile under that user's home.

**Impact:** limited to multi-user machines where another user's graphical session is open while this user runs migrations (`omarchy update` or `omarchy-migrate`) or `omarchy-provision-user`. There it fails on every retry. Under `omarchy update`, the migration failure triggers the update's error banner and stops the steps that follow it. In the installer step, later steps (mise, keyring, finalize marker) are skipped. Migrations are documented as running once for every user on the machine (`agents/skills/migrations.md`).

**Suggested change:** scope all three checks and the kill to the current user: `pgrep -u "$UID" -x fcitx5` and `pkill -u "$UID" -x fcitx5`.

This was shown with a stand-in that ignores SIGTERM, in the role of a process `pkill` cannot stop. It was not run with a second real user; the permission failure comes from procps source and `kill(2)` semantics.

## Paths that stop fcitx5 without starting it again

The helper stops fcitx5, but only the migration's success path starts it again. Three paths leave it stopped until the next login or `omarchy-restart-xcompose`:

- the installer step [`install/user/fcitx5-layout.sh`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/f58750fd1f19a793b106f857e6e844adeb0760c2/install/user/fcitx5-layout.sh), unchanged since the previous review (`omarchy-provision-user --force` in a live session: profile FR, unit inactive, no restart);
- a failed `write_profile` after the stop, also unchanged;
- the new `exit 1`: the migration aborts at line 11, before its restart (the unit stub stayed inactive, with 0 restart calls).

On these paths nothing starts fcitx5 again before the next login, despite the comment at lines 140-142.

**Impact:** fcitx5 input methods and compose sequences stay off until the next login or a manual restart.

**Suggested change:** have the helper start fcitx5 again on every exit once it has stopped or signalled it, when a graphical session is active (for example with an EXIT trap), and drop the migration's separate restart. This covers all three paths. It has not been tested.

**Optional test improvement:** no test case exercises the new branch, because every case sets the `pgrep` stub to report "not running". With lines 152-155 deleted, all 13 checks still pass. A case whose stub `pgrep` keeps matching, expecting a non-zero exit, no `changed` and an unchanged profile, passes at `f58750fd` and fails at `f28b2652` with `rc=0 out=changed`. The earlier suggestion to make the stop stub restore a stock US profile, which checks stop-before-write order, still applies.

**Still applies:** the `docs/file-layout.md:218-219` list still omits the fcitx5 layout seed. #12896, #11418 and #9565 are still open, and the earlier related-PR note is unchanged.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** follow-up limited to the new commit, its callers and the earlier findings. Sandboxed runs used real procps against fixture-owned stand-ins named `fcitx5`: one that saves 2 s after SIGTERM, one after 0.2 s, and one that ignores SIGTERM. The systemd user unit, `omarchy-restart-xcompose` and the session were stubbed. A second user was emulated, not run under a separate UID. Native fcitx5 was not re-run because the stop-then-write order is unchanged. The suggested code changes were not tested.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
